title: Exploratory transcription experiment completed without a qualifying checkpoint

data.title: Exploratory transcription experiment completed without a qualifying checkpoint
paragraphs: The separately authorized mixed-domain continuation finished at 4,000 optimizer updates after two consecutive validation checkpoints breached the saved retention limits. The supervisor retained step zero and the unchanged initial final model. Neither candidate qualified for use. No confirmation evaluation, refit, additional trial or automatic promotion followed. This result does not demonstrate a reliable broad transcription improvement, and it does not establish that single-dataset training would be better.

The run processed 20,225 example visits in 406.72 seconds of actual optimizer compute, approximately 6.78 minutes. It ended under the declared regression-based early-stop rule, before the maximum 10,000 updates, one-hour compute cap or full schedule pass. Actual visits were 6,433 Common Voice, 5,091 AMI, 2,985 CHiME 6, 1,703 VOiCES and 4,013 clean LibriSpeech. Distinct source counts were respectively 6,433, 5,091, 2,985, 502 and 3,408; repeated visits and microphone views are not independent utterances. Loading, compilation, native export and scoring account for additional wall time.

On the identical frozen exploratory development panel, WER percentages in initial / 2,000-update / 4,000-update order are: AMI 26.82 / 26.67 / 27.66; CHiME 6 76.32 / 76.52 / 76.66; CMU Arctic clean 8.54 / 8.27 / 8.63; older-speaker Common Voice 12.29 / 12.21 / 11.80; HiFiTTS clean 7.48 / 7.79 / 7.56; HiFiTTS native 6.46 / 6.77 / 6.92; LibriSpeech clean 5.89 / 5.29 / 5.61; LibriSpeech native 10.27 / 10.22 / 10.49; VOiCES 12.51 / 11.84 / 12.02. The nine-cohort macro WER is 18.51 / 18.40 / 18.59%; the equal-weight AMI/CHiME primary score is 51.57 / 51.60 / 52.16%. Lower values are better. Exact measurements and CER remain in validation_summary.json.

At 2,000 updates, the macro average improved by about 0.11 percentage points, with gains including clean LibriSpeech and VOiCES. However, the primary score did not improve, clean HiFiTTS worsened by 0.309 points beyond its 0.25-point limit, and the checkpoint was below the required 4,000-update exposure. At 4,000 updates, Common Voice, clean LibriSpeech and VOiCES still improved, but six of nine WER cohorts worsened. AMI rose by 0.831 points, exceeding its 0.5-point limit. These mixed outcomes support the saved rejection rather than claiming that every domain worsened or selecting the earlier macro average after the fact.

Quiet-speech WER was 31.82 / 31.99 / 34.06% on 160 microphone views, 77 source utterances and 1,004 reference words. The final increase of 2.233 percentage points exceeded the one-point quiet-speech limit. All three models inserted zero words on the same 20 fixed silence/Gaussian-noise probes. Passing those negative probes does not establish accurate quiet-speech transcription, and energy screening is not an intelligibility guarantee.

These are development point estimates from one bounded trajectory. No paired confidence intervals or confirmation comparison were produced because no nonzero checkpoint passed development selection. VOiCES development contains only 26 source utterances and HiFiTTS clean only two speakers; the unused confirmation panel has one HiFiTTS clean speaker. The CHiME populations appeared in earlier training or evaluation, so even a later qualifying result would have been exploratory. The evidence does not establish fresh independent confirmation, pretrained-base corpus independence, real product-microphone performance or an independent final age test.

The default native model remains C:\Users\amiri\Documents\GitHub\just-peachy\training\whistle_age_robust_v1\whistle.final.cact, with its original adapter.final.safetensors. The experiment's whistle.selected.cact and adapter.selected.safetensors are copies of that unchanged initial model; native SHA256 is cd6b10970450112a70f08cbf6416cac04462932be4604bda8f93b758f5b1c337. Rejected evidence checkpoints are preserved separately as whistle_transcription_guarded_v1/whistle.step_02000.cact (SHA256 4bcc46e44e243d8a8848a776ae4bc39e2307c64c17a1347de37976b3a8a56667) and whistle.step_04000.cact (SHA256 b0c43eefd14d731904b244ba3507ca6f6b3c1d804f6f2fe0a35d29c1c82cfd01), with corresponding adapters. No selected experimental artifact was published.

The pinned base weights and runtime retain Apache-2.0 provenance. Training-data attribution retains Common Voice CC0-1.0, AMI and VOiCES CC-BY-4.0, CHiME 6 CC-BY-SA-4.0 and the added clean LibriSpeech CC-BY-4.0 provenance. The user's CHiME 6 license confirmation remains resolved. The completed original and production campaigns and their distinct model identities are unchanged.

The experiment is complete and the initial model remains the default. Preserve the checkpoints, frozen evidence and this interpretation. Close this experiment's monitoring after successful report publication; no further training is authorized by this completion. The report's existing visual-review limitation remains: no approved renderer was available, its earlier installation was blocked, and this revision has not been visually inspected. Package/XML integrity checks do not prove page layout.
